extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners / attorneys and individuals subject to USPTO disciplinary processes
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, regulatory bases, procedural requirements, mitigating/aggravating considerations, and sanctions governing discipline of practitioners who are registered to practice patent law before the USPTO, as embodied in a USPTO Final Order resolving a settlement agreement with a respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction to discipline (statutory and regulatory basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over practitioner discipline pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions authorize the Director and OED to receive and act on settlement agreements, impose discipline, and carry out disciplinary proceedings under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, set forth at 37 CFR §§11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration to practice (e.g., Reg. No. 55,584) brings the practitioner within the scope of the Rules; violations of those Rules provide grounds for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional misconduct via state public discipline (37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Becoming publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a state constitutes professional misconduct under 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state supreme court suspension or public discipline (here, Wisconsin Supreme Court suspension) can trigger USPTO disciplinary action based on this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law misconduct definitions relied upon (SCR 20:8.4(c) and 20:8.4(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: SCR 20:8.4(c): 'It is professional misconduct for a lawyer to engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.' SCR 20:8.4(f): 'It is professional misconduct for a lawyer to violate a statute, supreme court rule, supreme court order or supreme court decision regulating the conduct of lawyers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State rule violations (e.g., failing to inform employer and allowing firms to believe exclusive employment) that constitute public discipline at the state level will be described in USPTO notices and support USPTO discipline under §11.804(h)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating considerations: acceptance of responsibility, remorse, and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's acceptance of responsibility for his actions, expressed remorse, and full cooperation with OED's investigation are relevant mitigating factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facts are cited in the Final Order and factor into the agreed-upon sanction — parties and OED routinely identify such mitigation when negotiating or imposing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director (or OED Director) may approve a Proposed Settlement Agreement submitted to the Under Secretary of Commerce for Intellectual Property and Director of the USPTO; the Agreement can resolve all disciplinary action arising from stipulated facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, agreed sanctions, and waivers of procedural rights; the Director's approval results in a Final Order implementing the settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction type and scope: suspension from practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may be suspended from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and non-patent matters for a fixed term (here, six (6) months), with an effective date (here, nunc pro tunc May 25, 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies the scope (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters), duration, and commencement date of the suspension; suspension terms can be negotiated in settlements and may be retroactive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to remain suspended until reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters until the OED Director grants Respondent's petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after the nominal suspension period lapses, reinstatement is a regulatory process requiring petition and OED approval per §11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 (cessation and affidavit obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58; Respondent submitted an affidavit comporting with §11.58 averring, inter alia, that he had ceased practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners subject to suspension must follow §11.58 notification/termination procedures (e.g., affidavit and cessation of practice) as part of compliance and discipline administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from CustomerNumbers and USPTO electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's name shall be dissociated from any CustomerNumber(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), and Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, nor have his/her name added to a USPTO Customer Number or a USPTO verified Electronic system account unless and until he/she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners are barred from maintaining or obtaining electronic credentials that enable practice before the Office until reinstatement is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements (FOIA Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of suspension showing name, registration number, suspension effective date, and the rule violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should include factual summary (e.g., state discipline basis and rule violations) and reference where the disciplinary decision is posted; publication is part of the public disciplinary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may consider disciplinary record in future matters (aggravating/rebuttal use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing further complaints or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding (i) as an aggravating factor, (ii) to rebut statements by Respondent, and/or (iii) in connection with any request for reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's prior discipline may be used to aggravate sanctions or counter representations in later proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural rights as part of settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may, and in this case did, waive rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. §11.56, waive the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. §11.57, and waive the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements commonly include express waivers of administrative and judicial review as a term of resolution; waiver binds the practitioner if knowingly made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certification of mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was certified as mailed by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, and transmitted by electronic mail to the Respondent; a Certificate of Service documents this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service of the Final Order on the respondent is required and is memorialized in a Certificate of Service included with the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent each shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may allocate litigation and compliance costs between the parties; here each party bears its own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct constituting underlying misconduct (employment-related dishonesty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to inform an (then) current employing law firm about commencing employment with a second law firm, performing client work for the second firm without the first firm's knowledge, and allowing both firms to believe the respondent was a full-time exclusive employee of each firm (including false denials) are behaviors that led to state discipline and support USPTO discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment concealment, unauthorized solicitation or representation of clients, and dishonesty to employers are factual behaviors that can trigger both state and USPTO discipline under dishonesty/misrepresentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with state discipline (concurrent/retroactive suspensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may seek that USPTO-imposed suspension run concurrently with a state court suspension; here the respondent ceased practice and requested concurrent/retroactive effect, and the Wisconsin Supreme Court imposed a retroactive six-month suspension effective May 25, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners and regulators may coordinate timing or seek retroactive/ concurrent effect between state and federal disciplinary sanctions; the Final Order reflects the outcome of those efforts.
